labels.label: prop:mesure_admissible
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: right, because the paper's statement covers every strongly causal E>=0-manifold and this file proves it only at M = E_0. The ledger regex finds no mark anywhere in the file, and the label is cited within the first 4000 characters. (1) E0.modelMeasures is an honest instance of Causal.Causality.ModelMeasures (Causal/SingularGeroch.lean:174). The structure asks, at each p, for an open U containing p, causally convex in the top open set, with an AdmissiblePastOn / AdmissibleFutureOn measure. Taking U = top is allowed by the definition and is exactly what timelikeLine_modelMeasures (:353) does. The instance is not vacuous: it carries proofs that muMinus is AdmissiblePast and muPlus is AdmissibleFuture on all of E_0, transported by admissiblePastOn_top / admissibleFutureOn_top. (2) E0.mesure_admissible is singularFlatAxioms.mesure_admissible isCausal modelMeasures, and nothing else. Its conclusion is the proposition's conclusion at E_0. isCausal, singularFlatAxioms, stronglyCausal and causallyArcConnected all resolve to the strict Causal.E0 declarations. BorelSpace E0 is Prod.borelSpace (checked with #synth). (3) Read literally against l.1737-1741. lam3_future: Regular, property 3 and property 4 in the future, for volume. lam3_add_lam1_past: the same in the past, for volume + lam1. lam3_past_profile: Regular and property 4 hold, property 3 fails (at (0,0) and (1,0) on the axis). All three match the AdmissibleFuture/AdmissiblePast fields (Causal/Measure.lean:93-114) one for one, property 2 left out as the paper leaves it out on the model. lam1 is the image of Lebesgue measure under tau -> (tau, 0), carried by the axis, which is sing_0 = singE0 0. (4) paper_measures_local is at least the paper's local form (l.1734-1743). In every neighbourhood N of every point p there is an open U with p in U, U inside N, closure of U compact, U causally convex in E_0, (volume + lam1).restrict U AdmissiblePastOn U, and volume.restrict U AdmissibleFutureOn U. The 'contained in a chart' clause is trivial at the model. (5) Measure-theoretic core, read and kernel-checked. measurePreserving_shear is a skew product of translations over id on C. lt_ray: ClosedLt (u+r1) r1 (u+r2) r2 0 unfolds to r1 < r2 and 0 < (r2-r1)^2, as the docstring says (E0Model.lean:376). frontier_ray_subsingleton_of_past/_of_future need only the <<-past/future closure property, so they hold for non-open sets too. volume_eq_zero_of_ray_subsingleton uses polar coordinates and Fubini. Together these make the frontier of any <<-past/future set lambda_3-null. Property 4: Jminus_diff_Kminus_subset gives (frontier I^-(A) minus axis) union (axis ∩ (J^-(A) minus K^-(A))). The second part is subsingleton because its points have tau = max over A of fcoord, attained (isGreatest_fcoord_of_mem_axis_inter, via le_axis_iff and mem_Kminus_of_lt_fcoord, both with Kminus_axis_eq / Kminus_eq_Iminus_of_not_mem_axis). axis_inter_Jminus_diff_Kminus_axis shows the singleton is attained. Null sets are taken for arbitrary sets: outer measure, and Mathlib's AbsolutelyContinuous quantifies over all sets, as rem:mesure_bord asks. (6) The class claim is true. admissiblePast/Future_of_equiv need IsFiniteMeasure plus mutual absolute continuity, and nothing else is used: regularity follows from finiteness on R x C, positivity on open sets and on axis segments is pulled back through the reverse absolute continuity, and nullity through the forward one. Measure.toFinite has the same null sets for an s-finite measure. lam1 is SFinite as a map of Lebesgue measure. (7) Question (which lambda_3, lambda_1): not open, and no OQ is needed. The Cartesian reading d tau dx dy and the coordinate reading d tau dr d theta = r^-1 d lambda_3 have the same null sets, are both locally finite (the integral of r^-1 times r dr is finite near the axis), and both charge open sets. Every parametrisation of the axis gives lam1 up to a constant. So admissible*_of_equiv (finite measures) and admissible*On_restrict_of (any mu << volume + lam1, positive on opens and axis segments, finite on V) cover every reading. The master should record it as a reading settled by the class result. (8) Observation for the planner, not checked and not a finding. For the general E>=0-manifold assembly, restriction_convexe in M gives J_{U_p} = J_M ∩ U_p. Transporting properties 3 and 4 from the model through a chart phi also needs J_{phi(U_p)} expressed through the model's own J: either a causally convex image in the model, or the local forms (pos_*_inter, null frontiers inside an open subset). At E_0 the chart is the identity and the question does not arise.

labels.label: rem:mesure_unilaterale
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: right, because the remark covers every causal E>=0-manifold with a BTZ line. E0.mesure_unilaterale is singularFlatAxioms.mesure_unilaterale isCausal singE0_zero_nonempty mu, nothing extra. The conclusion is the remark's 'no measure is admissible in the past and in the future at once', at E_0. mesure_unilaterale_sharp makes it non-vacuous: muMinus is AdmissiblePast, muPlus is AdmissibleFuture, and no measure is both. lam3_add_lam1_not_null_future is the remark's computation (l.1719-1722) at p = (0,0). axisSeg 0 1 lies in J^+(0) minus K^+(0) by Kplus_eq_Iplus, Jplus_axis and Iplus_axis: Iplus_axis asks 0 < rad, which fails on the axis. lam1 charges that segment. lam3_add_lam1_future_profile shows that, of properties 1, 3 and 4, exactly 4 fails in the future: 'property 4 is the obstruction' (l.1715-1716). The ledger note 'No witness with a BTZ point' is stale. It was already stale since E0.singularFlatAxioms (E0SingularFlat.lean:589); this file adds the measure-level witness.

findings.what: Finding 1 is correct and proof-level. lem:restriction_convexe (Causal/ArcConnected.lean:451-470) transfers J, I and K for A inside U. That gives property 4 on U_p at once, since J^-_U(A) minus K^-_U(A) = (J^-(A) minus K^-(A)) ∩ U. Property 3 on U_p instead needs mu((J^-(q) minus J^-(p)) ∩ U) > 0, which property 3 of the model does not give. pos_past_inter and pos_future_inter (MeasuresE0.lean:456, 483) are correct local forms, and they are what admissiblePast/FutureOn_restrict_of use. The Minkowski counterexample is right. Take mu finite and equivalent to lambda_3 restricted to {t < -1}. Property 3 in the past holds: p <= q with p != q forces q_t > p_t, and the slice of J^-(q) minus J^-(p) at t = s < min(p_t, -1) is a disk minus a smaller included disk, of area pi((q_t-s)^2-(p_t-s)^2) > 0. Property 4 holds because mu << lambda_3 and J^-(A) minus K^-(A) lies in the lambda_3-null frontier of I^-(A). Yet mu restricted to any U_p inside {t > -1} is 0. The paper's conclusion stands (it is proved at E_0); only the justification is short. Two problems with the REPORT's text. First, the suggested rewording covers the past sense only, while l.1742-1743 is about both senses. Second, 'only the paper's particular measures make the step true' overstates: every measure in their class works.

J^+(p)∖J^+(q)) meeting every neighbourhood of q (resp. p) in a non-empty open set or, in the past at a BTZ point, in a segment of the singular line, Lemma restriction_convexe turns ...'. Replace 'only the paper's particular measures make the step true' with 'the step uses where these measures put their mass (near q), not property 3 alone'.
